questions.enonce_markdown: An information system that processes instructions immediately as they arrive is termed
questions.corrige_markdown:
An information system is classified by the way it handles its input. A **real-time** system processes each input (transaction, sensor reading, instruction) **immediately as it arrives** and responds within a short, guaranteed time: air-traffic control, online seat booking and process control work this way.

A *batch processing* system, on the contrary, collects the data over a period and processes it all together later (payroll at the end of the month). A *Geographical Information System* stores and displays spatial data (maps) and a *Management Information System* summarises data to help managers take decisions; neither is defined by the immediacy of processing. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In SDLC, the collection of information by means of interviews , questionnaires, observation and inspection of documents is an activity in

*Options as printed:* A) System Analysis   B) System Design   C) System investigation   D) Information requirement
questions.corrige_markdown:
Interviews, questionnaires, observation and the inspection of existing documents are the **fact-finding techniques** used at the start of the systems development life cycle to learn how the present system works and what the users need. This is the work of the *investigation* (fact-finding) stage, which feeds the analysis of the problem; it is not design (design comes after the requirements are known) and "information requirement" is a result of the stage, not a stage of the life cycle.

The printed options overlap: many syllabuses call the whole fact-finding and requirements phase **system analysis**, others call its first part **system investigation**. Both A and C describe the same activity, so the question is not reliable for automatic marking. The wording of the question (collection of information) points at the investigation stage.

**Intended answer: C (System investigation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: When a code is compiled the outcome is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: The programmer writes **source code**. A compiler translates the whole source program into machine language and produces **object code**. A linker then combines the object code with library routines to build the *executable code*, and the *output* is what the running program displays. The direct result of the compilation is therefore the object code. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In designing a database, which diagram is used to represent real world situation into forms that can be unserstood by the DBMS
questions.corrige_markdown: The **Entity-Relationship (E-R) diagram** models the real world as entities (Student, Course), their attributes and the relationships between them. It is the usual first step of database design and is then converted into relational tables that the DBMS can store. A data flow diagram shows how data moves between processes in a system, not the structure of the stored data; the other two names are not standard database design diagrams. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How many computers can be used if we have 15 cables to put in a fullmesh topology ?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a full mesh every computer is linked directly to every other one, so $n$ computers need

$$
C = \frac{n(n-1)}{2}
$$

cables. We need $\frac{n(n-1)}{2} = 15$, i.e. $n(n-1) = 30$, so $n = 6$ ($6 \times 5 = 30$). Check: 5 computers need only 10 cables and 4 computers need 6 cables. A script confirms that $n = 6$ is the only solution (output: `[6]`). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A conversion method in which other modules are added incrementally is known as :
questions.corrige_markdown: Changeover (conversion) methods are: *direct* (the old system is stopped and the new one starts at once), *parallel* (both run together for a time), *pilot* (the whole new system is tried in one branch or department first) and **piecemeal** (also called phased): the new system is introduced **module by module**, each new module being added incrementally to the ones already in use. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the extended ASCII code. How many bits do we need to represent the word COMPUTER ?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Extended ASCII uses **8 bits (one byte) per character**. The word COMPUTER has 8 letters (C, O, M, P, U, T, E, R), so it needs

$$
8 \times 8 = 64 \text{ bits}.
$$

The option 56 comes from counting 7 bits per character (standard ASCII); 72 and 48 correspond to 9 and 6 characters. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which activity is done at every stage of the SDLC ?
questions.corrige_markdown: Coding belongs to the implementation stage only, design to the design stage, and analysis to the analysis stage. **Documentation** (recording requirements, design decisions, test results, user and technical guides) is produced and updated at every stage of the life cycle, so that the work can be understood, checked and maintained later. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Complexity of an algorithm is measured in terms of
questions.corrige_markdown: The complexity of an algorithm is the amount of resources it needs as a function of the size $n$ of its input: **time complexity** (number of basic steps executed) and **space complexity** (amount of memory used). The number of lines, loops or variables written in the program is not a measure of how the cost grows with the data. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of a universal gate
questions.corrige_markdown: A gate is **universal** when any Boolean function can be built using only that gate. The only universal gates are **NAND** and **NOR**. For NOR: $\overline{A} = A \downarrow A$; $A + B = (A \downarrow B) \downarrow (A \downarrow B)$; $A \cdot B = (A \downarrow A) \downarrow (B \downarrow B)$. AND, OR and XOR cannot produce an inversion on their own, so they are not universal. Among the options, only NOR qualifies. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Another name for a record in a database is :
questions.corrige_markdown: In the relational model a table is a *relation*, a column is an *attribute* (a field) and a row is a **tuple**, which is also called a **record**. A field is a single item of a record, a relation is the whole table, and an entity is the real-world object that the table describes. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The ___ locates and executes program instructions, carries out arithmetic operations, and fetches data from storage and input devices
questions.corrige_markdown: The **processor** (CPU) fetches instructions, decodes and executes them, performs arithmetic and logic operations and moves data between memory, storage and the input and output devices. RAM, registers and cache only *hold* instructions and data; they do not execute anything. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
If the capacity of a disc is 25GB, how many CDs can be used to store this quantity given that one CD has a capacity of 700MB ?

*Options as printed:* A) 36.57   B) 36   C) 37   D) 36.75
questions.corrige_markdown:
With the usual computing convention $1\ \mathrm{GB} = 1024\ \mathrm{MB}$:

$$
25\ \mathrm{GB} = 25 \times 1024 = 25\,600\ \mathrm{MB}, \qquad \frac{25\,600}{700} = 36.57\ldots
$$

A number of CDs must be whole and 36 CDs would hold only $36 \times 700 = 25\,200$ MB, so **37 CDs** are needed (the 37th is only partly filled). Script output: `25*1024/700 = 36.571..., ceil = 37`.

The printed question is ambiguous: with the decimal convention ($1\ \mathrm{GB} = 1000\ \mathrm{MB}$) the ratio is $25\,000/700 = 35.71$ and 36 CDs would be enough, while 36.57 is the unrounded ratio and an examiner may have wanted it. The most defensible answer to "how many CDs" is 37.

**Intended answer: C (37).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: If the processor is executing a main program that calls a subroutine, then after executing the main program up to the CALL instruction, the control will be transferred to the:
questions.corrige_markdown: A CALL instruction saves the return address (the address of the instruction that follows the CALL, usually on the stack) and then loads the program counter with the **address of the subroutine**, so that the next instruction fetched is the first one of the subroutine. When the subroutine ends (RETURN), control goes back to the saved return address in the main program. Control is not sent to the main program's start, nor to the CALL itself (that would loop forever), nor to a data address. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following allows many users to use the computer simultaneously?
questions.corrige_markdown: In a **time-sharing** operating system the processor time is divided into very short slices which are given in turn to the programs of many users connected through terminals, so each user has the impression of having the whole machine. A real-time system answers within strict time limits, a batch system runs jobs one after another without user interaction, and "interactive" only describes the dialogue between one user and the system. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following is NOT a memory performance parameter:
questions.corrige_markdown: The standard measures of memory performance are the **access time** (delay between a request and the data becoming available), the **cycle time** (minimum time between two successive accesses) and the **transfer rate** (amount of data moved per second). "Time location" is not a memory performance parameter. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that a node with two leaf nodes as children is deleted from a binary search tree, which note best replaces it in a strictly post-order tree transversal?

*Options as printed:* A) In order predecessor.   B) Post order successor.   C) Pre order predecessor.   D) Post order predecessor.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a binary search tree, a deleted node that has two children is replaced by a node that keeps the ordering of the keys: its **in-order predecessor** (the largest key of the left subtree) or its in-order successor (the smallest key of the right subtree). With two leaf children, the in-order predecessor is the left child and the in-order successor is the right child.

Of the printed options, "In order predecessor" is the standard textbook replacement rule. However, the words "strictly post-order" and the options are confused: the post-order predecessor of a node whose children are two leaves is its right child, which is also its in-order successor, so option D would work equally well. The question is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: A (In order predecessor).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A mathematical model with a collection of operations defined over its values is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: An **abstract data type (ADT)** is a mathematical model of a kind of data defined by its possible values and by the operations allowed on them, without saying how it is implemented (stack, queue, list). A *data structure* is a concrete way of implementing an ADT in memory, a *primitive data type* is one built into the language (integer, character), and an *algorithm* is a sequence of steps. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A complete binary tree with 2n+1 nodes contains:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A complete binary tree with an odd number of nodes has no node with a single child, so every internal node has exactly two children. Let $i$ be the number of non-leaf nodes and $\ell$ the number of leaves. Counting the edges two ways: $2i$ edges leave the internal nodes, and the tree has $(2n+1) - 1 = 2n$ edges, so $2i = 2n$ and

$$
i = n, \qquad \ell = (2n+1) - n = n + 1.
$$

So the tree has $n$ non-leaf nodes and $n+1$ leaves. A script that builds the heap-shaped tree for $n = 1, \ldots, 7$ gives (nodes, leaves, internal) = (3,2,1), (5,3,2), (7,4,3), ..., (15,8,7), which confirms it. The options use a capital N for the lowercase $n$ of the stem. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A sort which searches through a list to exchange the first element with any element less than it and then repeats with a new first element at subsequent positions is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The described method fixes the first position, looks through the rest of the list for an element smaller than it, exchanges them so that the smallest value ends up in the first position, then repeats the process with the second position, the third position and so on. This is the **selection sort** (select the minimum of the unsorted part and put it in place). Insertion sort inserts each element into an already sorted part, bubble sort swaps *adjacent* elements, and quick sort partitions around a pivot. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The data structure required to evaluate a postfix expression is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A postfix expression is read from left to right: each operand is **pushed** on a **stack**, and each operator **pops** the last two operands, computes the result and pushes it back. For example `2 3 4 * +` pushes 2, 3, 4, then `*` replaces 3 and 4 by 12, then `+` replaces 2 and 12 by 14. The last-in-first-out behaviour of the stack is exactly what is needed; a queue would give the operands in the wrong order. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The feature of the object oriented paradigm which explicitly helps code reuse is:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Inheritance** lets a new class take over the attributes and methods of an existing class and then extend or redefine them, so the existing code is reused instead of being rewritten. An object is just an instance, a class is a template, and aggregation builds an object out of other objects (it also supports reuse, but inheritance is the feature that is explicitly designed for it). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main advantage of a multiprogramming system is:
questions.corrige_markdown: In multiprogramming several jobs are kept in main memory and the processor switches to another job whenever the running job waits for an input or output operation. As a result more than one job is in progress at a time, the CPU is kept busy instead of idle, and the jobs as a whole are completed faster than if they were run one after the other. All three statements A, B and C are advantages. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: More than one job can be processed at a given time.

questions.enonce_markdown: An object encapsulates:
questions.corrige_markdown: Encapsulation means **bundling the data (state) and the methods that operate on it (behaviour) into one unit**, the object, and hiding the internal details behind a public interface. Data, behaviour or state alone is only half of the answer. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If a program in its functioning has not met user requirements in some way, then it is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Software testing terminology distinguishes: an **error** (a mistake made by a person), a **fault** or **defect** (the wrong instruction or design flaw that this mistake leaves in the program) and a **failure** (the visible deviation of the running program from what the user requires). A program that does not meet the user's requirements while it is running shows a **failure**. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is not true of a stack?
questions.corrige_markdown: A stack is an ordered list of items of the same type (A) with an overflow condition when it is full and an underflow condition when it is empty (B), and it offers `push()` and `pop()` (C). Both operations work at **one end only**, the top: this is the last-in-first-out rule. Statement D, with insertions and deletions at both front and rear at once, is false for a stack (it describes a double-ended queue). **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Ordered list of similar data type
Overflow state when completely full and underflow state when completely empty
Both push() and pop() are done at both front and rear simultaneously

questions.enonce_markdown: Dequeue() operation is best known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: On a queue, `enqueue()` adds an element at the rear and `dequeue()` **removes the element at the front**. "First in first out" is the name of the discipline of the queue, not of one operation, and the tail is the rear end. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Adding an element into a queue
Removing an element from a queue

questions.enonce_markdown: If there are no base cases in a recursive program, the program will:
questions.corrige_markdown: A base case is the condition that stops the recursion. Without it, each call makes another call and nothing ever stops the chain, so the program **runs indefinitely** (in practice until the call stack is full and a stack overflow error occurs). The program is accepted by the compiler, so it is executed (A is wrong). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Be executed until all conditions match

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is true of the characteristics of abstract data types?

i. A type

ii. A set of operations

Options give the truth value of (i) then (ii).
questions.corrige_markdown: An abstract data type is characterised by (i) **a type**, i.e. a set of values, and (ii) **a set of operations** defined on those values, independently of the implementation. Both statements are true. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following data structures can't store the non-homogeneous data elements?

*Options as printed:* A) Arrays   B) Records   C) Pointers   D) Stacks
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **record** groups fields of different types, so it can store non-homogeneous data. An **array** is a collection of elements that all have the same type; it cannot store elements of different types. This is the standard answer.

The printed question is however not clean: a stack is also described as a list of items of the same type in question 26, and a pointer only stores an address, so options C and D could also be argued. The question is not reliable for automatic marking.

**Intended answer: A (Arrays).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: It is a non-linear data structure?
questions.corrige_markdown: In a linear structure the elements are arranged in a sequence, each one having one predecessor and one successor (stacks, lists, strings). In a **tree**, an element can have several children, so the elements form a hierarchy: trees (and graphs) are **non-linear** structures. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number of comparisons done by a sequential search is?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a sequential (linear) search among $N$ items, finding the item in position $i$ takes $i$ comparisons. If the item is equally likely to be anywhere in the list, the average number of comparisons is

$$
\frac{1 + 2 + \cdots + N}{N} = \frac{N(N+1)/2}{N} = \frac{N+1}{2}.
$$

Check with a script: $N = 5$ gives 3.0 = (5+1)/2 and $N = 10$ gives 5.5 = (10+1)/2, whereas (N/2)+1 gives 3.5 and 6.0. The best case is 1 comparison and the worst case $N$. **Answer: B.**

A `for` loop tests its condition **before** each pass. Here $k$ starts at 0 and the condition is `k>9`. Since $0 > 9$ is false, the loop body is never executed and **nothing is printed**. A Python simulation of the same loop (`k=0; while k>9: print('Hello'); k+=3`) gives zero iterations (output: nothing).

The trap is to read the condition as `k<9`, which would give three passes ($k = 0, 3, 6$) and the output Hello Hello Hello (option C). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The postfix form of the expression (A+B)*(C*D-E)*F/G is?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Convert with the usual stack method, scanning from left to right, with `*` and `/` of equal priority and higher than `+` and `-`, and operators of the same priority taken left to right:

1. $(A+B)$ gives `AB+`.
2. $(C*D-E)$ gives `CD*E-` (the `*` is output before the `-`).
3. `(A+B)*(C*D-E)` gives `AB+CD*E-*`.
4. `*F` (same priority, left to right, so the first `*` is output first) gives `AB+CD*E-*F*`.
5. `/G` gives `AB+CD*E-*F*G/`.

This is option C. A script that implements the algorithm prints `AB+CD*E-*F*G/`. Option D is wrong (`CDE*-` means $C - D \cdot E$) and gives $-113.75$ for $A=2, B=3, C=4, D=5, E=6, F=7, G=8$ instead of 61.25. Options A and B evaluate to the same number only because of the associativity of multiplication; they are not the result of the algorithm applied from left to right. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Virtual memory is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Virtual memory is a technique in which the operating system keeps only the active parts (pages) of the programs in main memory and the rest on disk, moving them in and out as needed. The programmer sees a very large continuous address space, much larger than the real RAM: it is an **illusion** of an extremely large memory, not a real large memory. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: An illusion of an extremely large memory

questions.enonce_markdown: Concurrent processes are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Two processes are **concurrent** when their executions **overlap in time**: one starts before the other has finished. On a single processor they are interleaved (the processor switches between them); on several processors they may run truly in parallel. Option C is wrong because one processor cannot execute two processes at the very same instant, and concurrency does not require it. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Processes that do not overlap in time.
Processes that are executed by a processor at the same time.

questions.enonce_markdown: Fragmentation is:
questions.corrige_markdown: In paged memory, a process rarely fills its last page exactly; the memory words of that page that are **not used** are wasted. This wasted space inside allocated blocks is **(internal) fragmentation**. Dividing memory into equal fragments is paging, and the words that are used are not fragmentation. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Dividing the secondary memory into equal sized fragments.
Fragments of memory words used in a page.
Fragments of memory words unused in a page.

questions.enonce_markdown: A set of instructions that access common shared resources and exclude one another in time is best referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **critical region** (critical section) is the set of instructions of a process that access a common shared resource; the regions of different processes must exclude one another in time. *Mutual exclusion* is the **rule** that enforces this (only one process in its critical region at a time), *deadlock* is a state where processes wait for each other forever, and blocking only describes a process that waits. The question asks for the name of the set of instructions, hence critical region. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A key concept of quality control is that all products worked on:
questions.corrige_markdown: Quality control checks the outputs of a process against defined standards. For this to be possible, every product must have **measurable specifications for the outputs of the process**, so that an output can be measured and accepted or rejected. Delivery on time and within budget concerns project management, and documentation and testing are quality practices, not the defining concept. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Are delivered on time and within budget.
Have measurable specifications for process outputs.
Are thoroughly tested before delivery to the customer.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following data structures is used to hold jobs waiting to be run by the computer?
questions.corrige_markdown: Jobs must be served in the order in which they arrive: first come, first served. This first-in-first-out discipline is what a **queue** implements (the job queue or print queue of the operating system). A stack would serve the last job first, and a binary tree or a plain linked list does not impose this order by itself. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term module in the design phase of program development refers to:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the design phase a program is divided into small, self-contained parts called **modules**. A module can be a function, a procedure or, more generally, a subprogram: all three names refer to the same kind of unit. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is also known as a pre-order traversal of a binary tree where a given Node, has children Left and Right
In software engineering projects, what is informally called "SOFTWARE" consists of a:
questions.corrige_markdown: In software engineering, software is more than the programs: it is the programs (instructions), the **documentation** (specifications, design, user and technical guides) and the **operating procedures** that explain how to install and use the system. Programs alone, or programs with hardware manuals, are incomplete. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the state of the database no longer reflects a real state of the world that the database is supposed to capture, then such a state is called a(n).
questions.corrige_markdown: A database is in a **consistent state** when its content respects the integrity rules and reflects a real state of the world. When the stored data no longer reflect reality (for example, a transfer in which one account was debited but the other not credited), the database is in an **inconsistent state**. "Durable" is a transaction property (ACID), and there is no "parallel state". **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that if objects focus on real world entities of interest then we must be concerned with:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Object-oriented analysis** studies the problem domain and models the real-world entities of interest (customers, accounts, products) as objects. **Object-oriented design** then turns those objects into software objects (classes, interfaces, implementation structures). When the objects represent real-world entities, we are doing analysis. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A linear collection of data elements where the next node is given by means of a pointer is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a **linked list** each element (node) holds its data and a **pointer** to the next node, so the elements are linked in a sequence without being stored side by side in memory. "Node list" and "primitive list" are not standard names. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Software deteriorates rather than wears out because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Hardware wears out through physical ageing (heat, dust, friction). Software has no physical parts to wear, but it **deteriorates** over time: each change made during maintenance (new requirements, corrections) may introduce new errors in the way the components interact, so the quality of the software falls with the number of changes. Software is not affected by a hostile environment, use does not create defects, and it has no spare parts. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Software suffers from exposure to hostile environments.
Defects are more likely to arise after software has been used often.
Multiple change requests introduce errors in component interactions.
Software spare parts become harder to order.

questions.enonce_markdown: A main technique to make a software package portable is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: A portable program can be moved to another hardware or operating system with little change. The main technique is to **isolate the system-dependent components** (file access, screen handling, device drivers) in a small number of modules, so that only those modules have to be rewritten for a new platform. Performance does not make software portable, and a dependent platform is the opposite of portability. Option C describes what one would like to have, but it is not a technique that the developer applies to the package. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Have an independent platform for the software.
Have a dependent platform for the software.

questions.enonce_markdown: In system design, we do the following:
questions.corrige_markdown: System design covers both the hardware (computers, networks, devices) and the software (programs, files, interfaces) of the new system. The two designs depend on each other (the software needs the hardware performance and the hardware is chosen for the needs of the software), so they are done **in parallel**, not one strictly after the other, and hardware is not left out. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A factor in selection of a source language for program development is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The choice of the language in which a program is written depends on the skill of the available programmers, on the compilers and tools available for the language, and on the compatibility with the other software that the program must work with. All three are factors. **Answer: D.**
